brief.t: Formed in December 2018 when IDFC Bank merged with Capital First; IDFC Ltd merged into the bank in October 2024, so it now has no promoter.
Led by MD & CEO V. Vaidyanathan, re-appointed until December 2027; Sanjeeb Chaudhuri is Part-time Chairman.
FY 2025-26 net profit was ₹1,636 crore, after a ₹483 crore hit from a fraud at a Chandigarh branch in Q4.
Q2 FY27 (Jul–Sep 2026) profit nearly tripled (+196.5%) to ₹1,045 crore; customer deposits grew 26.9%.
Known for one of the highest margins among large banks: NIM 5.58% in Q2 FY27, with a CASA ratio near 48%.

timeline.t: IDFC Bank started operations, inaugurated by PM Narendra Modi.
Merged with V. Vaidyanathan's Capital First to form IDFC FIRST Bank.
Parent IDFC Ltd merged into the bank.
Raised about ₹4,876 crore from a Warburg Pincus affiliate as part of a ₹7,500 crore deal.
Got its first international credit rating, BBB- from S&P.

model.how: IDFC FIRST earns mainly from interest on retail, rural and small-business loans, which carry higher rates, funded by a large share of low-cost savings and current account deposits. This gives it a high net interest margin.
flow: Bank lends mainly to individuals, MSMEs and rural borrowers
Earns a wide interest gap + fees

points: RBI must approve a private bank's CEO and Chairman; IDFC FIRST's next Chairperson awaits RBI approval.
Newer private banks compete with HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank and Kotak for savings deposits.
Big theme for interviews: fraud control at branches, after the Chandigarh case.

frameworks.note: Framework views are analysis built from the verified facts on this page, not company statements.

glossary.Net profit: What is left after all costs, provisions and taxes. The bank's final earnings.
glossary.Net Interest Income: Interest earned on loans minus interest paid on deposits. A bank's main earning.
glossary.Net interest margin: Net Interest Income as a % of the bank's interest-earning assets. Shows how profitable lending is.
glossary.Gross NPA: Non-Performing Asset: a loan not repaid for 90+ days. Gross NPA is the % of all loans that have gone bad.
glossary.Net NPA: Bad loans after subtracting the money already set aside (provisions) for them. Lower is better.
glossary.CASA ratio: Share of deposits in Current and Savings accounts. These pay little interest, so a higher CASA means cheaper funds.
glossary.Capital adequacy ratio: The bank's own capital compared with the risk in its loans. RBI requires a minimum; higher means safer.
glossary.Provisions: Money set aside from profit to cover loans that may not be repaid.
glossary.Deposits: Money customers keep with the bank in savings, current and fixed deposit accounts.
glossary.Advances: Loans given by the bank to customers and businesses.
glossary.Dividend: Part of the profit paid to shareholders, per share.
glossary.Treasury gains: Profit from buying and selling bonds and other investments. It can swing a lot each quarter.
glossary.Attrition: The % of employees who leave in a year. Also called employee turnover.
glossary.RBI: Reserve Bank of India, which regulates all banks in India.
glossary.KYC: Know Your Customer: checking a customer's identity before opening an account.
glossary.MSME: Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises: small businesses that banks lend to.
glossary.Cross-sell: Selling an extra product (like a credit card) to an existing customer.
glossary.Public sector bank: A bank where the Government of India owns the majority of shares.
glossary.BRSR: Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report: an official yearly report on people, environment and governance that big listed companies must publish.
glossary.Reverse merger: When a parent company merges into its own subsidiary. IDFC Ltd merged into IDFC FIRST Bank in 2024.
glossary.Credit rating: An agency's grade of how safely a borrower can repay. BBB- is investment grade.
glossary.Unsecured loan: A loan given without collateral, such as a personal loan or credit card.

Role knowledge, the bank and HR questions

Finance.q: Why is IDFC FIRST's margin so much higher than other banks'?
Finance.a: It lends more to retail and small borrowers at higher rates and funds itself with a high share of low-cost CASA deposits.

Finance.q: Why did profit jump 196% in Q2 FY27?
Finance.a: The year-ago quarter was weak because of high provisions on microfinance; this year NII grew 21% and credit costs eased.

Marketing.q: IDFC FIRST pays good savings rates. How would you market that to young earners?
Marketing.a: Digital campaigns showing monthly interest credit, zero-fee features and an easy app, targeted at first-salary customers.

HR.q: How would you prevent branch fraud through people practices?
HR.a: Job rotation, maker-checker rules, ethics training, whistle-blower channels and strong supervision.

Sales.q: Sell me an IDFC FIRST savings account.
Sales.a: Ask about needs, then link interest rate, zero fees and app features. Close with a clear next step.

Operations.q: How can technology reduce fraud risk in branches?
Operations.a: Real-time alerts on unusual transactions, digital approvals and regular audits.

Other.q: What do you know about IDFC FIRST Bank?
Other.a: A private bank formed in 2018 by the IDFC Bank–Capital First merger, led by V. Vaidyanathan, with a high margin and fast growth.

It is still young enough that new joiners can make a visible difference. I want to grow with it and contribute to [your role].

gd.t: Should banks pay high savings rates to grow deposits?
gd.for: IDFC FIRST built a 47–50% CASA ratio this way.
gd.against: High deposit costs can squeeze margins.

gd.for: Loans growing 30% can hide future bad loans.
gd.against: Good underwriting and technology can grow safely.
